goal: Implement wrap(text, width) in word_wrap.py that greedily wraps words into lines of at most width characters, splitting over-long words and rejecting width below 1.
behaviors: wrap("", 5) returns "" and wrap("hello", 10) returns "hello" (a single short word stays on one line).
wrap("the quick brown fox", 10) returns "the quick\nbrown fox" (words are joined by single spaces and greedily packed onto lines of at most width characters).
wrap("a  b   c", 10) returns "a b c" (runs of spaces between words collapse to a single space).
wrap("abcdefghij", 4) returns "abcd\nefgh\nij" (a word longer than width is split into width-sized pieces).

wrap("hi abcdefghij yo", 4) returns "hi
abcd
efgh
ij yo" (the leftover piece of a split word starts a line that following words can join).
wrap("abc", 0) and wrap("abc", -3) each raise ValueError.

assumptions.text: word_wrap.py exists at the repo root as the single flat module.
The tests/ directory exists for the new test file.
pyproject.toml exists so the project toolchain is configured.
uv is available to run pytest in the project environment.
pytest can be run through uv without network access.

demo: python -c 'from word_wrap import wrap; print(repr(wrap("the quick brown fox", 10))); print(repr(wrap("abcdefghij", 4)))'
out_of_scope: Preserving newlines, tabs, or other whitespace beyond splitting on spaces
Hyphenation or smart breaking of long words
Unicode display width handling (width counts characters)

invariants.text: every line is at most width characters
invariants.check: all(len(line) <= args[1] for line in result.split("\n"))

invariants.text: greedy: no line has room for the first word of the line after it
invariants.check: all(len(a) + 1 + len(b.split(" ")[0]) > args[1] for a, b in zip(result.split("\n"), result.split("\n")[1:]))
